title: Scanopy
name: scanopy
description: Discovers the hosts, services and subnets on your network and draws them as topology diagrams that rebuild on every scan. Source: https://github.com/scanopy/scanopy

env.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or the server can't reach its database.

env.name: SCANOPY_PUBLIC_URL
env.label: Address you'll open Scanopy at
env.description: Used to build links. It must match the address in your browser, port included.

env.name: SCANOPY_LICENSE_KEY
env.label: License key (optional)
env.description: From Settings > License in Scanopy Cloud. Leave empty for the Community Edition.

note:
Set a database password before you deploy (openssl rand -hex 32 makes a good one). The stack won't start without it. Then open http://<your-host>:60072 and create your account. The first discovery starts on its own.

The scanning daemon runs with host networking and privileged mode, because ARP and ICMP discovery need raw sockets on the host's own network. It also mounts the Docker socket read-only, for Scanopy's Docker integration. Portainer admins can block privileged mode for regular users, so this template may only deploy for admins. Data is stored in the postgres_data, daemon-config and server-data volumes.

Integrations such as Docker, SNMP and UniFi add more discovery data, like containers and device details. Docs: scanopy.net/docs
